specification.problem: Determine whether a coined discrete-time quantum walk on a cycle-like graph achieves perfect state transfer (PST) between antipodal nodes, i.e. whether there is a step count t at which the walker, started at node 0, is found at node N/2 with probability exactly 1. The abstract studies this for modified versions of C4, C6, C8 and three coin operators, and reports generalised graph families with periodicity, PST or high-fidelity transfer.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction chosen by assumption (no experiment_scope supplied): the unmodified cycle C4 (N=4) with a coined DTQW using the degree-2 Grover coin (which equals Pauli X) and a flip-flop shift, with initial state localised at node 0. In this instance antipodal PST 0 -> 2 occurs at t=2 and the walk is periodic with period 4; this serves as the baseline against which the paper's cycle modifications are compared. Outside scope: the specific modifications of C4/C6/C8 that preserve PST, the identity of the three coin operators used in the paper, the three generalised graph families, the continuous-time walk results, interpolation between structures, and the decoherence model.

symbols.meaning: Number of nodes of the cycle C_N; antipodal node of 0 is N/2
Coin (direction) label: c=0 points to neighbour v+1, c=1 points to neighbour v-1 (mod N)
Coin operator acting on the coin register at each node (assumed identical at every node for the regular instance)
Flip-flop shift operator on the arc space
One step of the discrete-time quantum walk
Initial state, localised at node 0 with some coin state
Transfer fidelity: probability of finding the walker at the antipodal node N/2 after t steps

equations.label: Walk Hilbert space and state
equations.description: State of a coined DTQW on the cycle: position register tensored with a two-dimensional coin register (one coin state per neighbour of a degree-2 node).
equations.justification: Standard position-coin formulation of a coined discrete-time quantum walk on a 2-regular graph.
assumptions: Position register ordered first (most significant), coin register second
v encoded in binary with \lceil\log_2 N\rceil qubits

equations.label: Grover coin (degree d) and its degree-2 form
equations.description: Grover diffusion coin on a degree-d node (J_d is the all-ones matrix); at degree 2 it reduces to Pauli X.
equations.justification: The Grover coin is the standard choice for DTQWs on general graphs; the abstract mentions 'three choices of coin operator' without naming them, so Grover is adopted as an assumption for the instance.
assumptions: The Grover coin is one of the paper's three coins (not stated in the abstract)

equations.label: Flip-flop shift on the cycle
equations.description: Moves the walker to the neighbour selected by the coin and flips the coin so that it points back along the traversed edge (arc reversal). Addition is modular on \mathbb{Z}_N.
equations.justification: Flip-flop shift is the standard graph-independent shift for DTQWs on arbitrary graphs; it is an assumption that the paper uses it rather than a moving shift.
assumptions: Flip-flop (arc-reversing) shift rather than a moving shift

equations.label: Walk operator and evolution
equations.description: One DTQW step applies the coin at every node and then the shift; t steps give U^t.
equations.justification: Standard coined DTQW composition; node-independent coin assumed because the regular cycle instance has uniform degree.
assumptions: Same coin C at every node (valid for the regular cycle; modified cycles may need node-dependent coins)

equations.label: Antipodal transfer fidelity and PST condition
equations.description: Probability of finding the walker at the antipodal node after t steps (summed over coin states); perfect state transfer means this probability equals 1 exactly for some t.
equations.abstract_quote: perfect state transfer between antipodal nodes of discrete time quantum walks
equations.justification: The abstract states PST between antipodal nodes is studied; the vertex-occupation-probability definition of transfer fidelity is the usual one for DTQWs, but the paper's precise fidelity definition (e.g. whether coin state must also be transferred) is not given.
assumptions: Fidelity defined by position occupation probability, tracing out the coin

equations.label: Instance result: PST and periodicity on C4 with coin X
equations.description: With C=X and the flip-flop shift on C4 the walker moves persistently in one direction, reaching the antipodal node 2 exactly at t=2 (F(2)=1 for any initial coin state) and returning at t=4 (period 4). Equalities are exact.
equations.justification: Direct composition of eq_2, eq_3, eq_4 for N=4: X maps c to c\oplus1, then S moves to v+(-1)^{c\oplus1}=v-(-1)^{c} and flips the coin back to c. This is a baseline instance chosen by the reconstruction, not a result reported in the abstract.
assumptions: N=4, C=X, flip-flop shift, initial state localised at node 0

registers.name: position
registers.role: Encodes node v\in\{0,1,2,3\} of C4 in binary (v = 2 v_1 + v_0); most significant register in |v\rangle|c\rangle ordering

registers.name: coin
registers.role: Encodes direction c\in\{0,1\} (c=0: toward v+1, c=1: toward v-1 mod 4)

specification.initial_state: |\psi_0\rangle=|0\rangle_{\text{pos}}\otimes|0\rangle_{\text{coin}} (walker at node 0, coin pointing toward node 1); by eq_6 any coin state at node 0 gives the same antipodal transfer in this instance.

steps.description: Prepare the position register in |0\rangle and the coin register in |0\rangle.
Apply the coin operator C = X to the coin register (degree-2 Grover coin).
Apply the flip-flop shift: controlled on coin c=0 increment the position mod 4, controlled on c=1 decrement mod 4, then apply X to the coin register.
Repeat the coin and shift steps to reach the desired step count; for the C4 instance use t=2 (expected PST) and optionally t=4 (expected return to the initial state).
Measure the position register and estimate the antipodal occupation probability F(t).

specification.measurement: Measure both position qubits in the computational basis; the coin qubit may be measured and discarded. The outcome v=2 (binary 10) corresponds to the antipodal node; its frequency estimates F(t).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate F(t) as the fraction of shots with position outcome 2. For the C4/X instance the exact prediction is F(2)=1 and F(4)=0 with return to node 0; deviations beyond shot noise indicate circuit error. PST is declared when F(t)=1 within statistical tolerance.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied; the unmodified C4 with Grover (=X) coin and flip-flop shift was chosen as the smallest useful instance
The three coin operators in the paper are not named in the abstract; Grover was assumed for the instance
The flip-flop shift convention and position-first register ordering are reconstruction choices
Transfer fidelity is taken as antipodal-node occupation probability with the coin traced out

The paper's cycle modifications (added edges, self-loops, pendant vertices, weights, etc.) are unknown and were not reconstructed; the modified graphs would generally require node-dependent coin dimensions and a general arc-space formulation
missing_information: Which specific modifications of C4, C6, C8 were investigated and which few preserve PST
Identity of the three coin operators (e.g. Grover, Fourier/DFT, Hadamard are plausible but unstated)
Definition of the three generalised graph families and their node counts
Precise fidelity/PST definition used (coin-state transfer vs vertex occupation)
Continuous-time walk Hamiltonian (adjacency vs Laplacian) and transfer times for the families
Initial conditions (coin states) under which PST or high-fidelity transfer occurs on the modified graphs
Interpolation scheme between structures and the decoherence model used in robustness tests
